info.title: Halo: Combat Evolved
info.author: thelinkin3000
info.description: Halo: Combat Evolved, built from the decompilation of the Xbox game. Needs your own disc image.
info.details:
NOTE: Halo's game data is not included. Put an Xbox disc image of Halo: Combat Evolved (any version, .iso or .xiso) on the SD card as /switch/halo/halo.iso; the game unpacks its maps folder from it on the first start (about 1.7 GB on the card, a few minutes). Or put the disc's maps folder at /switch/halo/maps yourself.

Halo: Combat Evolved on the Switch, built from the decompilation of the Xbox game: the campaign, split-screen and online multiplayer, Halo Custom Edition maps (in /switch/halo/custom_maps), gyro aiming, and the game's own renderer on deko3d at up to 1080p docked.

Saves go in /switch/halo/save and the settings in /switch/halo/config.toml. The game updates itself from its GitHub releases when a new build is out.

changelog:
vbuild-132
Build 132: Faster Vulkan and compatibility with older phones!

- Vulkan: phones whose own Vulkan driver lacks dynamic rendering (Samsung's Mali phones, older Adreno phones such as the Nokia 8) now run the Vulkan renderer on that driver instead of falling back to OpenGL ES. A 48-bot match on a Galaxy S21 FE (Exynos 2100) runs at about 71 fps, where the open-source PanVK driver managed 33 to 39. (thelinkin3000)
- Vulkan: the renderer no longer makes the GPU finish all its work at every change of render target, which phone GPUs pay for most; on a Galaxy S21 FE with its own driver that took about a tenth off the GPU's time in a busy frame. (thelinkin3000)
- Vulkan: Video Setup's VULKAN DRIVER lists STOCK and then every driver archive in the freedreno_drivers folder by its name, including the Turnip build the app downloads for Adreno phones. TURNIP is gone from the list, and a vk_driver = "auto" left in config.toml becomes STOCK. (thelinkin3000)
- Vulkan: IMPORT DRIVER in Video Setup (Android, with VULKAN chosen) adds Vulkan driver archives (.zip) from your phone's files, checking each one is a driver first; it's listed the next time you open Video Setup. (thelinkin3000)
- Vulkan: if Vulkan can't start on your phone, the game sets GRAPHICS BACKEND to OPENGL, so Video Setup shows what's actually running. (thelinkin3000)
- Android: on phones whose CPU timer reports the wrong speed (the Galaxy S21 FE's Exynos 2100), the game no longer freezes: the main menu's background moves, a campaign loads after Choose Difficulty, and the menus keep responding after you create a profile. (thelinkin3000)
- Theater: on Android, IMPORT adds replays from your phone's files. (thelinkin3000)
- Mods: on Android, IMPORT adds a mod from a .zip of its folder, and DELETE deletes the selected mod after asking. (thelinkin3000)
- Saved games: checkpoints are kept in memory instead of written to storage, so a checkpoint no longer holds up the game's other reads and writes for seconds (most noticeable on Switch in co-op). (thelinkin3000)
- Replays and logs: the replay recording and debug.txt are written in the background, so writing them no longer drops frames (on Switch, a dropped frame every five seconds while recording). The overlay menu's System folder can turn off Write debug.txt and Write halo.log, on every platform. (thelinkin3000)
- Switch: a large write to the SD card no longer keeps the game's other reads and writes waiting until it finishes. (thelinkin3000)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 


Commit: https://github.com/thelinkin3000/halo-ce-universal/commit/72084314d9645ce6e968602dd263db8fe89c3cad
Build: https://github.com/thelinkin3000/halo-ce-universal/actions/runs/41403093808

The release builds are for playing; the debug builds stop at the first failed assertion and log it.

Build 111
- Switch and PS5: the main menu has no QUIT: the console's own Home or PS button leaves the game.
- PS5: each build has its own version number on the console, so stores and the console can tell that a newer build is an update.

Build 110
- Switch and Android: Halo's loading screen draws, the light sweeping over the Xbox's picture with its glowing trail; maps extracted by earlier builds get the picture from the disc image at the next start (on every platform).
- Switch: the first seconds after starting no longer freeze or cut the music, and the menus appear whole once their shaders are ready, behind the loading screen.
- Switch: when it looks for an update, the Switch also downloads the shaders of the campaign and of every multiplayer map (the shared shader keys), so a console compiles them in the background from its first start instead of as each map is first played.
- Switch: a map's load waits for its shaders under the loading screen, ten seconds at most, so a level's first moments are drawn whole; the loading screen's light now sweeps across the whole wait. Going back to the menus after a level no longer waits four seconds.
- Switch, Android and PS5: maps load sooner: the map is read from the card while it is unpacked (a campaign level about two seconds sooner on the Switch).
- Android and PS5: no more objects missing for the first frames of a map or a new effect: shaders compile on all the cores but two, and a draw whose shader is not ready compiles it itself, for up to a frame's time each frame.
